facts.raw_span: A 30-year-old man
asymptomatic, calcified mass on the right anterior maxilla
had been present for 18 months
mucosal fenestration through which a hard, mineralized structure approximately 1 cm in diameter was visible
periapical radiograph of the upper right premolar area demonstrated a discrete radiopaque lesion
initial diagnostic hypothesis was maxillary exostosis
incisional biopsy was performed to remove a fragment of the lesion
submitted for histopathological analysis

concepts.why: The presence of a calcified mass on the right anterior maxilla, mucosal fenestration with a hard mineralized structure, and a discrete radiopaque lesion on periapical radiograph are consistent with maxillary exostosis, which was also the initial diagnostic hypothesis.
The asymptomatic, calcified mass and discrete radiopaque lesion are also compatible with an odontoma, a type of odontogenic tumor that can present as a radiopaque mass in the jaw.
Although less likely given the maxillary location, a mandibular torus is a type of bony growth that could present similarly, with a hard, mineralized structure visible through a mucosal fenestration.
The presence of a calcified mass and discrete radiopaque lesion could also suggest an osteoma, a type of bony tumor that can occur in the jaw.
A compound odontoma is a type of odontogenic tumor that can present as a radiopaque mass in the jaw, consistent with the findings in this case.
